newsitem.title: USA: GFOA unhappy with Archer muni arbitrage proposal.
newsitem.headline: GFOA unhappy with Archer muni arbitrage proposal.

text.p: A Government Finance Officers Association official on Monday said the group was "very disappointed" with the arbitrage rebate relief provisions in U.S. Rep. Bill Archer's $85 billion tax plan.

Catherine Spain, director of association's federal liaison center, said the group was troubled that Archer's plan does not include two principal components of the arbitrage-rebate simplification package that the association recommended earlier this year.

One of the components of the association's package would establish a safe harbor from U.S. arbitrage rules for bond issuers that reasonably expect to spend 15 percent of bond proceeds within 12 months and 95 percent within three years of the issuance date.
Another key component would increase the rebate exemption for small issuers from those who reasonably expect to sell only $5 million of tax-exempt bonds in a year to $25 million.
The arbitrage provisions included in Archer's proposal "are not going to affect a lot of our people," a GFOA spokesperson said. They are just "housekeeping" changes to current rules, she said.
